choices.text: Because the heart burns blood like fuel
It cannot: blood is never used up, it loops back to the heart
Because the body makes new blood every minute

questions.feedback: That trap answer is the one to unlearn: The heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood. Reteach point: Blood is never used up: it keeps going round in a loop, coming back to the heart to be pushed around again. Check scene s3: follow one drop all the way round and watch it arrive back at the heart.
questions.misconception: The heart uses up the blood it pumps, so the body must keep making fresh blood.
questions.prompt: Why can the heart NOT use up the blood it pumps?

questions.feedback: Scene s2 fixes the picture: air travels down the windpipe, the lungs fill with air and grow bigger, then shrink as air flows back out.

questions.answer: It comes back to the heart and is pushed around the loop again.
questions.feedback: Scene s3 fixes the method: trace the drop out to the body and back again - the same blood returns to the heart, so it is never used up.
questions.prompt: What happens to a drop of blood after it has visited the body?
